summary: Blake lookout, Humboldt County: telephone lines in 1931 and 1933, a 1934 plan to move it to Cold Springs. FFLA lists the site gone; no source describes it today.

facts.status_note: Listed as a ground site that is gone; no source describes what remains.

visit.trail_note: PeakVisor says a trail called Last Chance Trail leads to the summit, 5,909 feet.

events.note: Telephone line from the Blake lookout to a ranch on the Mad River finished by a five-man crew
Forest Service telephone line linked the Mad River with Hyampom, the Blake lookout and Iaqua Buttes
Notice said the Blake lookout on South Fork Mountain would be abandoned and moved, with a Cold Springs lookout taking its place; the move is not confirmed

evidence.supports: 1931 telephone line finished, date of clipping
1931 telephone line built by a crew from Hayfork and Hyampom, running to a ranch on the Mad River
evidence.quote: A crew of five from Hayfork and Hyampom has finished building a telephone line from Blake Lookout to Peterson ranch on Mad Rover
The forest service has completed a new telephone line from Hinkley Range over the nearby ridges

evidence.supports: the 1933 line linked Hyampom, Blake lookout and Iaqua Buttes
evidence.quote: Hyampom, Blake lookout, and Iaqua Buttes

evidence.supports: 1934 notice: abandon and move, Cold Springs to replace it
evidence.quote: Blake lookout on South Fork mountain will be abandoned moved away. The new lookout at Cold Springs will take its place.

evidence.supports: Blake Mountain site is a ground site and gone
FFLA also lists a South Fork Mountain tower in Shasta County

evidence.quote: There's a trail called Last Chance Trail leading to the summit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts page dates the Times-Standard clipping September 21, 1976, but its text begins with 1933. The story uses 1933, the year the text describes.

notes_for_editor: Record is ground and gone with no build date, staffing or site description. The 1931, 1933 and 1934 items come only through the Forest Lookouts page that quotes them; the original newspapers were not checked. The 1934 notice names South Fork Mountain. Whether that is the same site as FFLA's Blake Mountain point (40.61424, -123.56070) is not confirmed. Two web searches found nothing specific to this lookout. Access and staffing are left out as unknown. PeakVisor's summit coordinates (40.614024, -123.561281) match FFLA's Blake Mountain point. The 1931 clipping spells the river 'Mad Rover'; the story uses Mad River. FFLA also lists a South Fork Mountain tower in Shasta County (40.65408, -122.52501), so the name alone does not link the 1934 notice to this site.
